name.text: Calculating the area of a field shaped as an irregular polygon.

questiontext.text:
The diagram below represents a field in the shape of an irregular polygon. A baseline AD is drawn, and perpendicular offsets are taken to vertices E and F.

  • Segments along baseline: AB = {@d1@} m, BC = {@d2@} m, CD = {@d3@} m
  • Perpendicular offsets: BE = {@h1@} m, CF = {@h2@} m
[[jsxgraph width="600px" height="300px"]] var d1 = {#d1#}; var d2 = {#d2#}; var d3 = {#d3#}; var h1 = {#h1#}; var h2 = {#h2#}; // Calculate absolute coordinates var xA = 0; var xB = d1; var xC = d1 + d2; var xD = d1 + d2 + d3; // Dynamic proportional scaling var totalW = xD; var maxH = Math.max(h1, h2); var ratio = 600 / 300; var spanX = totalW * 1.2; var spanY = spanX / ratio; // Ensure height fits gracefully if (spanY < maxH * 1.4) { spanY = maxH * 1.4; spanX = spanY * ratio; } var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, { boundingbox: [-spanX*0.1, spanY*0.8, spanX*0.9, -spanY*0.2], axis: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false }); // Points var A = board.create('point', [xA, 0], {name: 'A', fixed: true, color: 'black'}); var B = board.create('point', [xB, 0], {name: 'B', fixed: true, color: 'black'}); var C = board.create('point', [xC, 0], {name: 'C', fixed: true, color: 'black'}); var D = board.create('point', [xD, 0], {name: 'D', fixed: true, color: 'black'}); var E = board.create('point', [xB, h1], {name: 'E', fixed: true, color: '#1565c0'}); var F = board.create('point', [xC, h2], {name: 'F', fixed: true, color: '#1565c0'}); // Polygon Boundary board.create('polygon', [A, E, F, D], {fillColor: '#fff9c4', borders: {strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#212121'}}); // Internal Construction Lines board.create('segment', [A, D], {dash: 1, strokeColor: '#757575'}); board.create('segment', [B, E], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#d32f2f'}); board.create('segment', [C, F], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#d32f2f'}); // Right angle markers for offsets var rad = totalW * 0.03; board.create('angle', [E, B, A], {type: 'square', radius: rad, strokeColor: '#d32f2f', name: ''}); board.create('angle', [F, C, B], {type: 'square', radius: rad, strokeColor: '#d32f2f', name: ''}); // Clean Pixel-Gap Labels var gapY = spanY * 0.04; var gapX = spanX * 0.02; // Baseline labels board.create('text', [xB - d1/2, -gapY, d1 + " m"], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 14}); board.create('text', [xC - d2/2, -gapY, d2 + " m"], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 14}); board.create('text', [xD - d3/2, -gapY, d3 + " m"], {anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 14}); // Offset labels board.create('text', [xB - gapX, h1/2, h1 + " m"], {anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 14, strokeColor: '#c62828'}); board.create('text', [xC + gapX, h2/2, h2 + " m"], {anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 14, strokeColor: '#c62828'}); [[/jsxgraph]]

Calculate the total area of the field AEFD.

Area = [[input:ans1]] \(\text{m}^2\) [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To find the total area, we divide the irregular polygon into three simpler geometric shapes: two right-angled triangles and one trapezium.

1. Area of Triangle ABE (Left)

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \times {@d1@} \times {@h1@} \\ &= {@area1@} \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned} \]

2. Area of Trapezium BCFE (Middle)

The parallel sides are the offsets \(BE\) and \(CF\), and the perpendicular height between them is the baseline segment \(BC\).

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\ &= \frac{1}{2}({@h1@} + {@h2@}) \times {@d2@} \\ &= {@area2@} \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned} \]

3. Area of Triangle CFD (Right)

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \times {@d3@} \times {@h2@} \\ &= {@area3@} \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned} \]

Total Area

Add the three areas together:

\[ \begin{aligned} \text{Total Area} &= {@area1@} + {@area2@} + {@area3@} \\ &= {@ta@} \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned} \]

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: You forgot the \(\frac{1}{2}\) factor. Both the triangle formula and the trapezium formula require you to multiply by \(\frac{1}{2}\).
You treated the entire field as a single large trapezium. You must calculate the area of the two triangles and the central trapezium separately, then add them together.
